MEASUREMENT AND LIMITS
Logical size is the sum of file lengths by pathname, including hidden files. Folder counts are recursive file counts; child folders are not counted as files. Parent/child rows overlap and must not be summed. The complete directory tree includes empty folders. The root also includes files directly in C:\DATASTORE.
SQLite discovery examined the first 16 bytes of every readable, non-reparse regular file >=16 bytes, in addition to database filename candidates. No models, Parquet records, JSON data payloads or credentials were decoded by the filesystem scan. Directory reparse points are recorded rather than followed outside scope. Any enumeration/signature errors appear below.
Database allocation is GetCompressedFileSizeW: Windows-reported allocated data size for that pathname, including compression/sparse effects where supported, excluding filesystem metadata. It is not a measure of unique physical storage across hard links. WAL, SHM and rollback-journal files are measured separately. Absent sidecars contribute zero at their observation time, not a promise they cannot appear later.
SQLite inspection used URI mode=ro&immutable=1, query_only, memory temp storage, schema/PRAGMA metadata and aggregate row-count/payload-length queries only. This avoids journal/shared-memory creation and reads the main database without WAL. Schema/page results therefore exclude any uncheckpointed WAL. The audit is not an atomic filesystem snapshot or corruption check; concurrent external changes may occur. Main-file size/mtime changes during each DB inspection are reported.
October 27-29 selection uses Windows creation time OR last-write time in America/Los_Angeles, from 2026-10-27 00:00 through 2026-10-30 00:00, limited to the scan observation. Creation time can reflect copying/restoration. Current lengths are not bytes added during those days. No prior comparable size baseline was available; growth is not calculated.
Purpose and use claims distinguish concrete selected Scout source/launch bindings, remaining code capabilities, and lack of an identified consumer. CRITICAL DIFFERENCE FROM CHECKOUT / ATLAS ASSUMPTIONS
Current installed Scout independent services use ServiceStore, which puts full scientific objects in external content-addressed JSON and compact envelopes in SQLite. CHECKOUT ml\intraday\store.py still shows the generic inline ShadowStore implementation. It would be incorrect to describe Scout solely from that checkout or to assume Atlas uses Scout's installed extension.
INSTALLED\ml\intraday\live_session.py:618-621 selects ServiceStore for the independent trading role, otherwise ShadowStore.
INSTALLED\ml\intraday\scout_services.py:349-358 opens C:\DATASTORE\intraday\shadow.sqlite3 with _ModelServiceStore/ServiceStore and C:\DATASTORE\intraday\services as object/spool root. Lines 489-492 open services\preparation.sqlite3 with the same object root and also open shadow.sqlite3 for evidence.
CHECKOUT\ml\intraday\store.py:125-138 stores full encoded payloads inline in snapshots. CHECKOUT\ml\intraday\runtime.py:349-369 constructs full X, y, inference and candle snapshots; 409 saves full model result in events; 421 puts model outputs in forecast payload. Those are implementation options, not proof of Atlas's deployed bytes or data contents. Inspect Atlas's selected/loaded release and actual schema before drawing deletion conclusions.

TRAINING SNAPSHOTS AND REFERENCES
1. Current 1A preparation executes the same scientific builder and freeze path but stops before fitting or publication (INSTALLED\ml\intraday\runtime.py:457-492). Each snapshot includes X, y, inference_X, inference, feature names, label-availability/reference/target-close arrays, manifest, cutoff, dataset scope and source manifest. The candles member includes observations from the loaded history with availability <= cutoff and opening <= reference; it is not independently limited here to the estimator's newest-row cap (lines 474-484). The inference snapshot also carries its trailing observation subset (INSTALLED\ml\intraday\data.py:1375-1404).
2. ServiceStore.freeze_inputs serializes that whole snapshot canonically, hashes the bytes, writes services\objects\<snapshot hash>.json, then separately writes a full indicator object in the same folder and places only a bounded indicator projection plus object path/hash/witness into SQLite snapshots. symbol_inputs links cycle/symbol to snapshot ID (INSTALLED\ml\intraday\service_handoff.py:352-400).
3. ReadySpool publishes a compact ready envelope both to services\manifests\<ready ID>.json and the ready table in services\handoff.sqlite3 (service_handoff.py:179-223). Those two representations duplicate a small manifest, not the full matrix/history.
4. System 1B PreparedHistories.load verifies that referenced full object and calls store.attach with the same envelope, so preparation.sqlite3 and shadow.sqlite3 share an external scientific object rather than writing separate full histories for the same published snapshot (INSTALLED\ml\intraday\scout_services.py:200-222).
5. Exact-byte hashing deduplicates identical complete objects only. Cutoff and reference are part of snapshots (runtime.py:457-463); later reference/cutoff values change the hash even when nearly all rows are unchanged. There is no row/chunk/delta history deduplication in this persistence path. Thus full overlapping history and matrices are retained repeatedly across distinct snapshots. This source finding does not measure actual duplicate-byte totals.
6. Retries reuse the first frozen input for the same cycle/symbol. Ready publication reuses a previous exact source-session/envelope manifest (service_handoff.py:183-193). New source sessions and changed timestamps can create additional immutable records. Ready queue retirement changes status to expired or superseded; it does not delete rows, manifests or scientific objects (service_handoff.py:226-242). A bounded active queue therefore does not mean bounded total on-disk history.
7. Historical inline SQLite snapshots remain supported. INSTALLED\ml\intraday\store.py:137-144 recognizes the external envelope schema and otherwise validates an inline dict. New external storage did not imply migration/removal of older inline history. Whether and how much inline data remains is for the parent's metadata-only DB audit.

FITTED MODELS AND RESULT REPRESENTATIONS
INSTALLED\ml\intraday\runtime.py:250 defaults artifacts to C:\DATASTORE\intraday\models. It makes a new UUID attempt ID and uses cycle-prefix/symbol/attempt as a run directory (530-538).
INSTALLED\ml\intraday\models.py:561-575 writes each artifact using joblib into a temporary file, publishes the final immutable file by a hard link, then removes the temporary name. Normally this leaves one final file; temporary and final links during publication are not two independently allocated model copies.
models.py:643-650 gives each model output its own metadata: model spec, training cutoff, feature names, a training-data hash, dataset metadata, fitting/calibration evidence and dependency versions. models.py:683-685 writes {estimator, metadata, version} into <model name>.joblib. Full X/y are not separately included as explicit top-level arrays by this exporter; an estimator may itself retain training information as part of fitted state. No model was deserialized during this audit.
The same completed result information has multiple deliberate representations:
- Full fitted result, including per-model metadata/diagnostics, is serialized inline in shadow.sqlite3 events as models_completed (runtime.py:543; generic event writer store.py:175-178).
- Forecast construction includes fitted outputs again (runtime.py:555), and ServiceStore saves the full scientific forecast to another content-addressed services\objects JSON (service_handoff.py:430-436).
- shadow.sqlite3 forecasts stores a separate compact forecast: summary manifest and model name/status/probability/version/timing fields plus hash/path/witness to the full scientific forecast; its contract caps execution JSON at 64 KiB (service_handoff.py:438-457).
- Model metadata is also embedded in each joblib artifact. Full estimators are not put into SQLite by this code.
Distinct fit attempts get distinct directories, and the live runtime does not deduplicate/reuse fitted artifacts merely because the training matrix hash is unchanged. Full scientific outputs differ with timing and attempt/artifact metadata as well. A completed forecast for the same immutable cycle is reused; failed/interrupted attempts may retain separate artifact evidence. Busy-write retry code specifically retries original evidence writes rather than replaying completed model work (INSTALLED\ml\intraday\scout_services.py:253-335).

MOST LIKELY SPACE-AMPLIFICATION MECHANISMS, TO COMPARE WITH MEASURED FOLDER SIZES
1. Whole overlapping training snapshots and used historical candles retained per distinct reference/cutoff, without chunk/delta deduplication.
2. Full model output metadata repeated in events and scientific forecast objects and each model artifact.
3. New complete model artifacts for distinct cycle/attempts.
4. Immutable raw request receipts alongside canonical raw+normalized stock storage, plus actual-response journals and derived observation stores.
5. Append-only scientific/queue evidence despite bounded currently-ready working sets.
These mechanisms are established by source. They do not establish which actual bytes are redundant, removable, or responsible for October 27-29 growth. Only metadata inventory and an earlier comparable baseline could quantify growth.

- S\ml\intraday\market_collection_adapters.py:415 chooses responses/<date>/<request-identity>.json; :417-421 reuses a completed response after checksum verification; :424 creates a UUID .dbn under raw/<date>; :427 captures the native request; :432-440 retains raw path/hash/size evidence even on failures. - S\ml\intraday\market_collection.py:852-882 removes exact duplicates WITHIN one received result only. :888-905 builds a source/window/receipt/availability envelope containing records and provider evidence. :907-916 writes a new immutable snapshots/<quarter date>/<task>/<UUID>.json then indexes it. The per-attempt timing/status/provenance can differ even when some values repeat.
- S\ml\intraday\market_collection_index.py implements receipts.sqlite3 as a query/discovery index; the source receipts still supply validated content. Index metadata and payload files are not the same complete store.
- S\ml\intraday\market_collection_history.py:229-277 handles historical cache identity, completed response verification, and DBN files under historical. This is bounded historical market-depth evidence separate from native current capture.
- Context-cache-<symbol>.sqlite3 files are derived feature-vector caches (S\ml\intraday\live_model_recipe.py:677). docs/development/intraday-market-data-contract.md:194-202 documents their disposable-cache semantics.
